Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
703 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Tweaked temperatures down further in many areas outside the
major cities overnight with temperatures falling steadily.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and warm conditions expected through Saturday.

- 2) Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks up 
the Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and warm conditions expected through
Saturday.

Surface high pressure remains overhead through Saturday 
resulting in dry conditions and calm winds. Highs will be above 
average with temperatures in the 60s to even the low 70s this 
afternoon through Friday. Clear skies and light winds overnight 
yield favorable conditions for radiational cooling. Overnight 
lows will drop into the 30s tonight with lows Thursday and 
Friday night staying in the mid 30s to 40s. 

While remaining overhead, surface high pressure begins shifting
northward on Saturday as a low pressure system develops off the
coast of Florida and tracks north. This results in increased
cloud cover although dry conditions and calm winds persist.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks up 
the Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday. 

An area of low pressure is forecast to develop off the Southeast 
U.S. coast late this week, then track north to northeast along the 
coast this weekend. The low's initial forward speed is going to be 
slow as it gets trapped underneath a brief, weak upper ridge, then 
quickly picks up speed as it moves northeast with a strong upper 
trough approaching from the OH Valley. There remains considerable 
differences among the global guidance, both run to run and between 
models in each run. The ensemble guidance for both the European and 
GFS remain quite dispersive with low tracks well inland across the 
NC/VA Piedmont to well offshore of the Mid-Atlantic. Of particular 
interest are the Euro and GFS AI models that are more in line with 
each other, both indicating a low track between I-95 and the 
coastline. The low pressure quickly deepens and rapidly tracks 
toward southern New England and Nova Scotia Monday into Monday 
night. 

At this time there remains too much uncertainty to pin down any 
specific details or impacts to our area. Rain chances Sunday into 
Sunday night have steadily increased, especially east of the Blue 
Ridge. This is in line with the more westward tracks of the GEFS. 
The exact track of the low is going to be critical to where the 
heaviest rain falls, though there could be a sharp gradient on the 
western side of the precip shield from heavy to very light rain 
amounts. It is worth mentioning the higher-end of the ensemble 
spread indicates 2-4" as a worst-case scenario, but many members 
also have little to no rain for most of the area - this probably 
speaks the best to how much uncertainty remains. The location 
of the heaviest QPF also varies greatly from along US-15 to the 
Delmarva. Continue to monitor the forecast over the next few 
days as guidance hopefully starts to converge on a solution for 
this weekend. 

A strong Canadian High builds across much of the central to eastern 
CONUS during the early part of next week. This is going to bring us 
dry, brisk, and much colder conditions. Models are indicating the 
potential for another coastal low moving through the region around 
the Thanksgiving holiday.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
VFR conditions and calm winds persist through Saturday as high
pressure remains overhead. Some fog may try to develop
particularly near rivers/bay early Thursday, but confidence on
impact at any one TAF site is low. Light winds out of the south
to southwest are expected through tomorrow with winds becoming 
light and variable overnight. On Friday, winds shift to 
northwesterly before shifting to southeasterly on Saturday. We 
continue to monitor the developing coastal low off the coast of 
Florida. As this low pressure system drifts northward, 
precipitation and sub-VFR conditions are possible across the 
terminals with the greatest chances being eastern terminals.

&&

.MARINE...
Light and non-hazardous winds continue through Saturday. A low 
pressure system is forecast to develop off the coast of Florida 
and may bring precipitation and increased winds to the waters on
Sunday. Winds may near SCA criteria on Sunday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
High pressure will move directly overhead and remain there over
the next few days. Expect warming temperatures and very dry air
to take hold as a result. While winds will remain low, RH 
values will go down substantially. Overnight recoveries, 
especially on the ridges, will be very poor as well starting 
tonight. Expect afternoon RH values to drop well into the teens 
and 20s each day west of the Blue Ridge, and the 20s to 30s east
of the Blue Ridge. This will also be paired with seasonably 
warm temperatures, so this will really act to dry out already 
very dry fuels. While fire will be slow to move due to lack of 
wind, very dry air will make for easy fire starts, so exercise 
extreme caution in the coming days. 

Not helping matters is that there is no precipitation expected 
east of the Appalachians through at least the end of the week. 
Given the setup, will really be watching for any potential dry 
frontal passages in the long range as the next days to really 
watch out for. Still watching late weekend into early next week 
for the next weather system, but unsure what it will bring at this
point. While precipitation chances have increased a bit over the
past several days, it is still not a certainty by any means. 
Should the areas miss out on substantial precipitation from this
system, there could be some fire weather concerns early next
week with dry frontal passage. Continue to monitor the latest 
forecast as this timeframe approaches.
